# OmniDB Documentation

## Overview

OmniDB is an open source browser-based app designed to access and manage many different Database Management systems: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, MS SQL Server, Firebird and SQLite. Its user interface is available in English, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese and Korean. OmniDB can run either as a desktop app or via browser, combining the flexibility needed for various access paths with a design that puts security first. The backend was fully rewritten from Python/Django to Go in 3.6.x, and the desktop shell has migrated from NW.js to Wails; the old Python-based plugin system (pglogical/BDR/Postgres-XL support) was removed in that rewrite and is not coming back — see the Legacy Features & History page.

---

## Introduction

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/introduction.html

**Description:** Introduction to OmniDB - a browser-based database management tool supporting PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL, MS SQL Server, Firebird, and more. Features a unified workspace, background execution of queries and procedures across multiple databases, and encrypted data storage.

**Key Topics:**
- History and origins of OmniDB
- Multi-DBMS support
- Security features
- 2025-2026 revival; backend fully rewritten from Python/Django to Go in 3.6.x

## Additional Features

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/additional_features.html

**Description:** Smaller features: the Welcome page, the Getting Started tutorial, contextual PostgreSQL documentation, Properties/DDL panels, data export (desktop Save dialog vs. browser download), Export as DBML, query history and SSH terminal connections.

**Key Topics:**
- Welcome page and Getting Started walkthroughs
- Contextual help (Doc: ...)
- Properties and DDL panels
- Export tools (CSV, TSV, XLSX, JSON, XML, Markdown)
- Export as DBML: PostgreSQL database schema export in the token-efficient DBML format, well suited for giving an LLM/AI assistant schema context
- SSH console (Terminal connections)

## OmniDB Config Tool

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/omnidb_config_tool.html

**Description:** The old Python-era `omnidb-config` GUI tool no longer exists; this chapter documents the manual equivalents (SQLite app-database location, default admin user, setting/resetting a user password with `omnidb-server --set-password`, resetting/vacuuming the database).

**Key Topics:**
- App database location
- Default admin user
- Resetting a lost password (`--set-password`)
- All omnidb-server command-line options (see Deploying omnidb-server)
- Manual config equivalents

## Monitoring Dashboard

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/monitoring_dashboard.html

**Description:** The Monitoring section: a per-connection live dashboard of 17 built-in native units (16 PostgreSQL, 1 MySQL) plus custom units driven by a single SELECT query (Grid, Chart (No Append), Timeseries); units start paused; Enable All/Pause All, card size, and the Manage Units side panel for showing, hiding and ordering units.

**Key Topics:**
- Monitoring section and shared connection tabs
- Built-in units (PostgreSQL/MySQL)
- Manage Units panel
- Writing custom units as a single SQL query

---

## Notify

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/notify.html

**Description:** The Notify section: listening to PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY channels, Oracle DBMS_ALERT alerts and Firebird events per connection; adding, pausing and deleting channels; filtering and clearing messages; automatic stop with Restart Listening; sending test notifications with SQL.

**Key Topics:**
- Supported engines (PostgreSQL, Oracle, Firebird)
- Channel management and persistence
- Message list, filters, ephemeral messages
- Test NOTIFY / DBMS_ALERT.SIGNAL / POST_EVENT examples

---

## Connected Users

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/connected_users.html

**Description:** The Connected Users section: live sessions/backends of PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server and Firebird servers, per-engine columns, system processes toggle, query text pane with Open in a new Query tab, and terminating sessions.

**Key Topics:**
- Per-engine session columns
- Viewing a session's current query
- Terminating a session
- Replaces the former Backends/Process List/Sessions tree menus

---

## Roles and Permissions

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/permissions.html

**Description:** The PostgreSQL Permissions section: a Miller-columns browser of roles (including the PUBLIC pseudo-role), direct and inherited role memberships, and effective object privileges (direct, inherited and via PUBLIC); creating, altering and dropping roles, granting/revoking memberships and object privileges.

**Key Topics:**
- Roles column: Create Role, Alter Attributes, Change Password, Drop Role
- Members / Member of, Grant Membership, Add Member, Set as Active Role
- Effective privileges tree for databases, tablespaces and schema objects
- Edit Privileges dialog: direct vs. inherited privileges, With grant option
- PostgreSQL only; actions execute immediately

**Key Topics:**
- Replication setup
- Publication management
- Subscription management

---

## Deploying omnidb-server

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/deploying_omnidb-server.html

**Description:** Deploying and configuring OmniDB server — a single Go binary with no configuration file, no separate websocket process and no built-in TLS; all command-line options (-A, -H, -p, -d, --set-password) and a reverse-proxy setup that forwards a loopback Host header.

**Key Topics:**
- Command-line options
- Binding address and port
- Reverse proxy setup for TLS termination (Host header, X-Forwarded-Proto)

---

## Security and Multi-user Server

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/security.html

**Description:** How OmniDB protects saved credentials and a multi-user server: AES-256-GCM encryption of saved passwords with the key in the OS secret store (or a .connection_secret_key file), the one-time initial admin password, sign-in lockout (10 failures / 15 minutes), session invalidation, server-mode restrictions for SQLite and PostgreSQL file parameters, public connection protections, per-user exports, SSH host key verification via known_hosts, and loopback Host allowlist.

**Key Topics:**
- Encryption of saved passwords at rest
- Initial admin password and --set-password
- Sign-in lockout and sessions
- Server-mode restrictions (SQLite, PostgreSQL connection-string parameters)
- Public connections and exports
- SSH known_hosts requirement
- TLS, reverse proxy, DNS-rebinding protection

---

- Ace editor shortcuts
- Multicursor editing

---

## Legacy Features & History

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/legacy_features_and_history.html

**Description:** OmniDB's version timeline, and what happened to its removed Python-based plugin system — including the pglogical, Postgres-BDR and Postgres-XL plugins — the removed PL/pgSQL step debugger, and the removed Advanced Object Search feature, after the 3.6.x rewrite from Python/Django to Go. Links to the original unmaintained repository for anyone who still needs an old release with plugin support.

**Key Topics:**
- Version history (original ASP.NET/C# project → Django → 2025-2026 revival → Go rewrite → Wails migration)
- Why the plugin system, pglogical, Postgres-BDR and Postgres-XL support were removed and are not returning
- Why the PL/pgSQL step debugger was removed (never ported to Go, and fundamentally incompatible with managed/cloud PostgreSQL)
- Why Advanced Object Search was removed (dead code calling functions that no longer existed, never functional since the Go rewrite)
- Where to find old releases (github.com/OmniDB/OmniDB, github.com/OmniDB/plugins)

---
